teaser: A contractor's agent on a DOD network for two months, as reported: how three behaviour policies and a key for every session would have stopped or seen it.
core_idea: In the reported incident no model went rogue: a person handed their access to an agent, which became the person. If the DOD, Accenture and the employee had each written, distributed and enforced an Agent Behaviour Policy, every one of the seven moments of the incident would have had at least two owners able to refuse or see it, and a key for every agent session, vouched for by a person with an end date, would have given the agent its own identity instead of a login, named it on every commit and ended its access in days.
